questions.question: In semiconductor memory architecture, why do Dynamic Random-Access Memory (DRAM) cells require periodic refresh cycles, whereas Static Random-Access Memory (SRAM) cells do not?
options: DRAM utilizes floating-gate transistors that gradually trap oxide charges during read operations, requiring periodic electrical erasure.
DRAM relies on dynamic CMOS domino logic gates that must be precharged during every second clock phase to avoid logic contention.
DRAM stores data as an electric charge on a tiny capacitor that naturally discharges over time due to leakage currents, whereas SRAM uses cross-coupled inverters that actively hold their state.
DRAM employs magnetic domain wall tracks that require periodic current pulses to keep magnetic bits aligned with pinning sites.
DRAM operates without sense amplifiers, meaning reading a bitcell drains the internal battery rails unless refreshed externally.

questions.question: In digital logic synthesis and synchronous circuit optimization, what is the operational principle of 'retiming'?
options: Relocating sequential storage elements (flip-flops/latches) across combinational logic gates to balance path delays without altering external input-output behavior.
Dynamically scaling the master clock frequency and supply voltage at runtime in response to varying computational workloads.
Inserting pipeline registers exclusively at module input/output boundaries to reduce routing congestion in the physical floorplan.
Replacing single-cycle multicycle paths with multi-threaded execution units in the processor microarchitecture.
Swapping high-leakage low-threshold voltage (LVT) standard cells with high-threshold voltage (HVT) cells to reduce static power dissipation.

questions.question: In modern high-performance microprocessor front-ends, what is the primary architectural purpose of a dedicated Return Address Stack (RAS)?
options: To buffer outstanding store addresses in program order so that loads can bypass data before committing to L1 cache.
To record target addresses for indirect jump instructions that depend on runtime register values computed in the ALU.
To track speculative instruction pointers during an exception recovery sequence to restore the architectural program counter.
To accurately predict subroutine return target addresses by pushing the return address on function calls and popping it on returns.
To store the historical execution trace of taken/not-taken outcomes for conditional branches in a circular shift register.

questions.question: In ASIC physical design and power integrity analysis, what is the fundamental physical distinction between static IR drop and dynamic IR drop?
options: Static IR drop occurs strictly in flip-flop clock trees, whereas dynamic IR drop affects only combinational logic standard cell rows.
Static IR drop is caused by average steady-state DC current flowing through interconnect resistance, whereas dynamic IR drop is caused by peak transient currents during simultaneous cell switching.
Static IR drop arises from electromigration voids in metal wires, whereas dynamic IR drop is driven by electrostatic discharge (ESD) events during I/O switching.
Static IR drop is caused by capacitive coupling between adjacent signal lines, whereas dynamic IR drop is caused by inductive ground bounce across package bond wires.
Static IR drop only impacts designs operating in subthreshold regions, whereas dynamic IR drop occurs exclusively when transistors enter saturation.

questions.question: In domain-specific hardware accelerator design (such as tensor processing units), what is the defining structural and computational characteristic of a 2D Systolic Array?
options: Instructions are broadcast in lockstep to thousands of independent ALUs sharing a massive unified multi-bank register file.
Independent compute threads communicate exclusively via an asynchronous crossbar network using packet-switched routing protocols.
Each processing core dynamically fetches instructions from a private instruction cache and commits results out-of-order via a reorder buffer.
Operands are prefetched from off-chip DRAM into dedicated scratchpad SRAM memories before being evaluated sequentially by a single SIMD vector unit.
Data flows rhythmically through a regular grid of interconnected processing elements, allowing data to be reused locally among neighbors without repeated memory or register file accesses.
